The two parameters from the REACH Regulation used to distinguish scientific research and development from product-oriented research and development in the AI Act are:

1. The scale of the R&D activity: Scientific research and development involves quantities 'less than 1 tonne per year', 'under controlled conditions', and 'at a laboratory scale', whereas product-oriented research and development can occur in either 'a pilot plant' or in 'full-scale production'.

2. The purpose of the R&D activity: Product-oriented research and development aims at 'product development or the further development of a substance', whereas scientific research and development aims at 'experimentation, analysis', 'monitoring and […] diagnostics'.
